newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of India plans 6.75 bln rupee IPO in February.
newsitem.headline: Bank of India plans 6.75 bln rupee IPO in February.

text.p: The Bank of India, one of India's leading state-run banks, announced its maiden public issue of 6.75 billion rupees on Tuesday.

Bank chairman G. Kathuria said the offer price for the initial public offer (IPO) would be 45 rupees per share of 10 rupees in face value. The issue will open for subscription in the last week of February, he told a news conference.

He said the bank had emerged as the highest profit-making bank among all state-run banks last year, with a net profit of 2.76 billion rupees. It recorded a net profit of 2.11 billion rupees for the six months ended September 30, 1996, he said.
The bank has projected a net profit of 4.0 billion rupees for the year ending March 31, 1997, Kathuria said.
"Personally, I think it would be much higher -- between 4.5 to 5.0 billion rupees this year," he said.
The bank expected to follow up the IPO with an issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) later in 1997, he said.
The bank's capital adequacy was currently 8.44 percent.
The government holding would fall to 76.52 percent after the IPO, Kathuria said. The government has authorised the bank to reduce its holdings in the bank upto a maximum of 49 percent.

"The bank's annualised EPS based on the first half year results for 1996/97 (April-March) works out to 8.63 rupees on the adjusted capital, indicating a price earning multiple of 5.21 for its issue price," the bank said in a statement.

There is no reservation for foreign financial institutions in the proposed issue. After reservations for Indian financial institutions, banks, expatriate Indians, mutual funds and employees, the net offer to Indian public would emount to 3.15 billion rupees, the bank statement said.
